extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent attorneys, and patent office personnel in Turkey
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from the Turkish patent code covering rights, scope of protection, application formalities, search/examination, objections, priority, fees, and third‑party rights. Useful for applicants and practitioners preparing, prosecuting, or challenging patents in Turkey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farmer's right to use patented breeding or animal reproduction material
rubrics_metrics.description: The farmer has a right to use the patented breeding or other animal reproduction material provided from the patentee; or sold by his permission; or obtained by another commercial way for agricultural purposes. This tenancy covers the use of animals or other in order to maintain their own agricultural strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tenancy is subject to the provisions of Law number 5042. Procedure and rules regarding the use of this right shall be determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use must not harm law, morals, or public order
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of the patent shall not be used in a way that will cause harm for the law, morals, and public order. This use shall also be bound up with current or future definite or indefinite‑statutory prohibitions and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prevent indirect use via supply of essential factors or equipment (Article 86)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee has the right to prevent the supply/release to third parties of factors or equipment that constitute the basis of the invention and make its practice possible, to parties who do not have authority to use the patented invention, where the third parties are aware (or it is sufficiently clear) that such factors/equipment are sufficient to use the invention and are being used for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the factors/equipment are ordinary market products available at all times, Paragraph 1 shall not be applied where third parties do not induce unauthorized parties to practice the invention. Persons performing acts authorized by Article 85(3) subparagraphs are not considered unauthorized under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by previous domestic use (Article 87)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who used the invention domestically in good faith on or before the application date, or persons against whom serious and real measures were taken for their use, may continue using the invention in the same way or begin using it in accordance with the measures taken, to the extent necessary to meet the reasonable needs of their business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The right remaining from previous use cannot be expanded by issuing a license and can only be transferred together with the business. Practices regarding products offered for sale by such persons are outside the scope of the patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use by state monopoly holders and related takeover/compulsory measures (Article 88)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent concerns subjects in the field of activity of state economic enterprises with monopolistic goods/services, allowing the monopoly right holder to use the invention depends on the patentee’s permission. The monopoly right holder may claim permission or the patentee may ask the monopoly holder to take over the patent; price is to be agreed or determined by court if parties fail to agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monopoly holders are obligated to use inventions that provide considerable economic benefits and significant technical progress in their sector. If monopoly arises after grant, the patentee may claim the monopoly holder also take over the business/facility using the invention; court determines price if no agreement. If the invention cannot be used due to a legal monopoly, annual patent fees need not be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims determine extent of protection; use of description and drawings in interpretation (Article 89(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of protection provided by the patent application or the patent itself shall be determined by claims. The description and drawings shall be used in interpreting the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on claim interpretation and prohibition on impermissible extension (Article 89(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not be interpreted strictly by literal word meaning, but when determining extent of protection claims must not be extended to cover ideas thought of by the inventor but not claimed, nor to cover features expected to arise merely by interpreting the description/drawings beyond the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should not be broadened to capture unclaimed subject matter implied by description beyond what a skilled person would reasonably derive as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced interpretation to protect patentee and give third parties certainty (Article 89(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are interpreted to provide the applicant/patentee with the protection they deserve and to give third parties a reasonable level of positive assertion about the extent of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of published claims and retroactivity limits (Article 89(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection provided by the application is determined by the published claims of the application until the patent is granted. The situation of the patent when granted or after objection/invalidity procedures shall determine retroactive protection, provided the protection scope is not extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents considered in scope (Article 89(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors equivalent to those mentioned in the claims at the time of alleged infringement are also considered in determining protection. An element is equivalent if it functions in the same way, meets the same functional requirements, and leads to the same conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/patentee statements and samples in claim interpretation (Article 89(6)‑(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: During procedures determining claim extent, applicant or patentee’s statements shall be considered. If the patent includes samples, claims shall not be limited to such samples; products or methods should not be excluded merely because additional features are not present in samples or samples do not cover all specified objectives/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents for patent application and confirming application date (Article 90(1)‑(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must include: (a) application form; (b) description explaining the invention; (c) claims; (ç) the drawings referred in description/claims; (d) abstract; (e) payment information. The application date is confirmed when the request for granting a patent, applicant identity/contact, and a description (in Turkish or permitted languages) or a referral to a previous application are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description, claims, abstract and drawings may be submitted in Turkish or in the language of a Paris Convention/WTO party or reciprocity countries; further procedural rules by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of genetic source or traditional knowledge (Article 90(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is based on a genetic source or traditional knowledge related to the genetic source, the patent application must explain where the source was obtained from.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship and entitlement statements in application (Article 90(5)‑(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor shall be declared in the application but may request anonymity. If the applicant is not the inventor (or only some inventors), they must explain how they obtained the right to file. The inventor has a right to request to be declared as inventor and have their name included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and rules regarding applications determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention and divisional application requirements (Article 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must relate to a single invention or a group of inventions forming a single general inventive concept. Applications not meeting this requirement may be divided. Divisional applications may be filed regardless of unity, but must not go beyond the subject matter of the earlier application; divisional retains original application date and priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual fees remaining from past years must be paid with divisional. Divisional applications not filed in accordance with this article are not admitted for processing; further rules by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure and biological material deposit rules (Article 92(1)‑(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be explained by a person skilled in the art in a very clear and complete way that enables practical application using the drawings, description and claims. If the invention involves biological material not publicly available and not definable sufficiently by a skilled person, the invention is considered sufficiently explained on condition the material is deposited/entrusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entrusted biological material later becomes unavailable, re‑entrustment in accordance with the Budapest Treaty and submission of the deposit certificate copy within four months is required to maintain uninterrupted deposit. Requirements regarding entrusted biological material are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of claims, clarity and not exceeding description (Article 92(4)‑(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of the claims shall be the description; claims must define the subject to be protected, be clear and concise, and must not go beyond the invention as defined in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract is for providing technical information only and must not be used to determine extent of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right entitlement and scope (Article 93)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who filed an application for the same invention in any Paris Convention or WTO party country may claim priority in Turkey within 12 months of the first filing. Exhibitions recognized under the Paris Convention may also give priority within 12 months of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National equivalents, bilateral/multilateral agreements or Code provisions may extend entitlement; the priority date has effect for certain articles (e.g., Article 83 and Article 109). The date of a national application filed in due form is treated as the application date regardless of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority: time limits and scope (Article 94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority must be claimed (with fee) together with the application or within two months of the application date; supporting documents must be submitted within three months of application date. Multiple priority claims allowed; priority covers only subject matter included in the earlier application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority may nevertheless cover specific invention features not present in the later claims if clearly disclosed in the original priority application as a whole. Detailed procedures by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary formal compliance analysis and correction windows (Article 95)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that lacks required elements (per Article 90(3)) will not be processed. If deficiencies exist, applicant may correct or submit Turkish translation within two months of the application date; failure leads to withdrawal. The Office analyzes admitted applications for conformity with other formal conditions and may require correction within two months or refuse the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consistent with formal conditions, a search report will be prepared pursuant to Article 96.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search request timing, preparation and reasons for not preparing search report (Article 96)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must request a search (and pay the fee) with the application or within 12 months from the application date; failing that, the application is considered withdrawn. If the application is consistent with formal conditions, the search report is prepared, the applicant notified and the report published. If the subject falls under Article 82(2)&(3) or unclear description/claims prevent preparation, no search report is prepared and the applicant is asked to submit objections or make changes within three months; failure results in refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council of Ministers authorized to reduce the 12‑month period by half; procedures by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of application and interim effects (Article 97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon expiration of 18 months from application or priority date the patent application/utility model is published. From publication date third parties may present comments regarding patentability, though they are not part of the Office's processing at this phase. Protection under the Code is temporarily entitled to the applicant as of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person who used the invention without permission is informed of the application and its extent, the temporary protection applies even before publication. For microorganisms, protection starts after the microorganism becomes available. If the application is withdrawn/considered withdrawn/rejected, these effects are treated as not having occurred. Rules by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination request, office examination and amendment/response deadlines (Article 98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must request examination (and pay fee) within three months of notification of the examination report, otherwise application is withdrawn. The Office examines conformity with the Code; if non‑conformity is found the applicant is notified and may present opinions or make changes within allotted time; such notifications cannot be repeated more than three times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant allotted three months from notification to respond or make changes; failure results in withdrawal. If examination finds conformity, the patent is decided to be granted and published. If changes are required to grant, the Office will ask for changes within two months; failure to make/confirm changes results in withdrawal. A granted patent is not a guarantee by the Office of validity or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for third‑party objection after grant and objection evaluation (Article 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may object (with fee) within six months from publication of the patent grant decision on grounds: (a) subject does not comply with patentability conditions (Articles 82 & 83); (b) invention is not sufficiently disclosed per Article 92(1)‑(3); (c) patent subject exceeds scope of the first version of application or previous versions (e.g., divisional bases). Objections must comply with regulation conditions and fee/timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no objections are made or considered not made, grant decision is finalized. Office notifies patentee who has three months to comment or amend. The Board evaluates and may uphold the patent, declare nullity (published and nullity consequences apply), or partially maintain and invite required changes within two months; failure leads to nullity. Final decisions published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to object to Office decisions (Article 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applicants, patentees or related third parties may object to Office decisions within two months from notification; such objections are evaluated by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of protection and annual maintenance fees (Article 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent protection runs 20 years from application date; utility models 10 years; these periods are not extendable. Annual fees for maintaining the patent/application are due at the end of the second year and annually thereafter, payable on the month/day corresponding to application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual fees may be paid with surcharges within six months following the due date. Failure to pay within that time causes expiration as of the due date; Office will notify and publish expiration. Payment of compensatory fee within two months of the expiration notification can revalidate the patent as of the payment date but revalidation cannot interfere with third parties' acquired rights. Notification of expiration must be made no later than one year from due date; consequences and third‑party rights determined by court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and analysis of unpublished patent applications by third parties (Article 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not yet published patent applications cannot be analyzed by third parties without written permission of the applicant. Exceptions: third parties who can prove that the patentee intends to use the rights provided by the application against them may analyze the unpublished application without permission. Also, if a divided application or a new patent application filed under certain provisions is published, the previous application can be analyzed by third parties prior to its publication and without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and rules regarding third‑party analysis of patent applications are determined by regulation.
